verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 52.8
verses.english: Linked Discourses 52.8

verses.pali: 1. Rahogatavagga
verses.english: 1. In Private

verses.pali: Salaḷāgārasutta
verses.english: The Salaḷa Tree Hut

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ āyasmā anuruddho sāvatthiyaṁ viharati salaḷāgāre.
verses.english: At one time Venerable Anuruddha was staying near Sāvatthī in the salaḷa tree hut.

verses.pali: Tatra kho āyasmā anuruddho bhikkhū āmantesi …pe… etadavoca:
verses.english: There Venerable Anuruddha addressed the mendicants:

verses.pali: “seyyathāpi, āvuso, gaṅgā nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā.
verses.english: “Reverends, suppose that, although the Ganges river slants, slopes, and inclines to the east,

verses.pali: Atha mahājanakāyo āgaccheyya kudālapiṭakaṁ ādāya:
verses.english: a large crowd were to come along with a spade and basket, saying:

verses.pali: ‘mayaṁ imaṁ gaṅgānadiṁ pacchāninnaṁ karissāma pacchāpoṇaṁ pacchāpabbhāran’ti.
verses.english: ‘We’ll make this Ganges river slant, slope, and incline to the west!’

verses.pali: Taṁ kiṁ maññathāvuso, api nu so mahājanakāyo gaṅgānadiṁ pacchāninnaṁ kareyya pacchāpoṇaṁ pacchāpabbhāran”ti?
verses.english: What do you think, reverends? Would they succeed?”

verses.pali: “No hetaṁ, āvuso”.
verses.english: “No, reverend.

verses.pali: “Taṁ kissa hetu”?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: “Gaṅgā, āvuso, nadī pācīnaninnā pācīnapoṇā pācīnapabbhārā.
verses.english: The Ganges river slants, slopes, and inclines to the east.

verses.pali: Sā na sukarā pacchāninnaṁ kātuṁ pacchāpoṇaṁ pacchāpabbhāraṁ.
verses.english: It’s not easy to make it slant, slope, and incline to the west.

verses.pali: Yāvadeva ca pana so mahājanakāyo kilamathassa vighātassa bhāgī assā”ti.
verses.english: That large crowd will eventually get weary and frustrated.”

verses.pali: “Evameva kho, āvuso, bhikkhuṁ cattāro satipaṭṭhāne bhāventaṁ cattāro satipaṭṭhāne bahulīkarontaṁ rājāno vā rājamahāmattā vā mittā vā amaccā vā ñātī vā sālohitā vā bhogehi abhihaṭṭhuṁ pavāreyyuṁ:
verses.english: “In the same way, while a mendicant develops and cultivates the four kinds of mindfulness meditation, if rulers or their chief ministers, friends or colleagues, relatives or family should invite them to accept wealth, saying:

verses.pali: ‘ehambho purisa, kiṁ te ime kāsāvā anudahanti?
verses.english: ‘Please, my friend, why let these ocher robes torment you?

verses.pali: Kiṁ muṇḍo kapālamanusañcarasi?
verses.english: Why follow the practice of shaving your head and carrying an alms bowl?

verses.pali: Ehi hīnāyāvattitvā bhoge ca bhuñjassu puññāni ca karohī’ti.
verses.english: Come, return to a lesser life, enjoy wealth, and make merit!’

verses.pali: So vata, āvuso, bhikkhu cattāro satipaṭṭhāne bhāvento cattāro satipaṭṭhāne bahulīkaronto sikkhaṁ paccakkhāya hīnāyāvattissatīti—netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
verses.english: It is quite impossible for a mendicant who is developing and cultivating the four kinds of mindfulness meditation to resign the training and return to a lesser life.

verses.pali: Taṁ kissa hetu?
verses.english: Why is that?

verses.pali: Yañhi taṁ, āvuso, cittaṁ dīgharattaṁ vivekaninnaṁ vivekapoṇaṁ vivekapabbhāraṁ taṁ vata hīnāyāvattissatīti—netaṁ ṭhānaṁ vijjati.
verses.english: Because for a long time that mendicant’s mind has slanted, sloped, and inclined to seclusion. So it’s impossible for them to return to a lesser life.

verses.pali: Kathañcāvuso, bhikkhu cattāro satipaṭṭhāne bhāveti, cattāro satipaṭṭhāne bahulīkarotīti?
verses.english: And how does a mendicant develop and cultivate the four kinds of mindfulness meditation?

verses.pali: Idhāvuso, bhikkhu kāye kāyānupassī viharati …pe…
verses.english: It’s when a mendicant meditates by observing an aspect of the body …

verses.pali: vedanāsu …pe…
verses.english: feelings …

verses.pali: citte …pe…
verses.english: mind …

verses.pali: dhammesu dhammānupassī viharati ātāpī sampajāno satimā, vineyya loke abhijjhādomanassaṁ.
verses.english: principles—keen, aware, and mindful, rid of covetousness and displeasure for the world.

verses.pali: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu cattāro satipaṭṭhāne bhāveti, cattāro satipaṭṭhāne bahulīkarotī”ti.
verses.english: That’s how a mendicant develops and cultivates the four kinds of mindfulness meditation.”

verses.pali: Aṭṭhamaṁ.
